history.new: Low confidence. Streaming width is essentially the one-way communication complexity of the t-step local rule used by Durr-Rapaport-Theyssier (TCS 322 (2004) 355-368, https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0210008; their d_n uses the central cut and the maximum over the two directions). They classify ECAs into bounded/linear/other and prove linear complexity with an explicit description of f^n for rule 132 (Lemma 10), so 'unbounded width yet easy prediction' is already exemplified there. The fuse magma and its burn-time fast-forward were not found (Historian audit 2026-10-19, reviews/historian_C11_C20.md).
history.old: Searches (2026-10-18) on CA prediction complexity, branching-program/light-cone complexity and computational irreducibility (Wolfram; Israeli-Goldenfeld, arXiv:nlin/0309047; Moore's prediction papers) found no notion of streaming width of t-step rules and no analysis of this rule; the burn-time mechanism itself is elementary. Small.

statement:
For the fuse magma [[0,0,0],[0,0,1],[1,2,2]] (0 burnt, 1 burning, 2 intact): burn times satisfy tau_i = 0 (x_i = 0),
tau_(i+1) + 2 (x_i = 2), tau_(i+1) (x_i = 1, x_(i+1) = 2), 1 (x_i = 1, x_(i+1) != 2); the row at any time t is
obtained from them in O(L) operations; and floor((m+1)/2) <= lambda(t) <= 3t + 3 with m = floor(t/2), so the
streaming width grows linearly (computed lambda(t) = t + 2 for t <= 12).
title: The fuse magma: linear streaming width, yet an O(L) fast-forward for every t
